paragraphs: Friend, listen to how Jesus starts. His first word to the crowd is BLESSED (Matthew 5:3). He doesn't open with a to-do list or a scolding. He opens by telling the poor in spirit, the mourners and the meek that the kingdom of heaven, comfort and the earth are theirs (Matthew 5:3-5).

Then He gets personal. He says, "Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of Me" (Matthew 5:11). And He tells them, "Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven" (Matthew 5:12). That tells me following Jesus can cost something, and the reward is bigger than the cost.

And look what He calls His listeners: "You are the salt of the earth" and "You are the light of the world" (Matthew 5:13-14). He doesn't say try to be. He says you ARE. So don't tuck that lamp under a basket, because He says it belongs on a stand, giving light "to everyone in the house" (Matthew 5:15). Let it shine so people see your good deeds and "glorify your Father in heaven" (Matthew 5:16), and the glory goes to Him, not to you.
